terms.meaning: the costs of running the business other than the direct cost of goods sold
a named group of related costs
the yearly percentage rise in prices

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It explains the two ways expenses are calculated and loads the helper tools.
sections.why: Gives the reader the formulas before the code.

sections.name: calculate_opex_percent_revenue
sections.title: Operating cost as share of revenue
sections.what: Multiplies each year's revenue by a percentage to get that year's cost for the category.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a cost grow with sales, which is how some expenses usually behave.
sections.watch_out: The percentage must be a decimal such as 0.15, not 15.

sections.name: calculate_opex_fixed
sections.title: Fixed operating cost growing with inflation
sections.what: Starts from a base amount and grows it year by year using the inflation rates.
sections.why: Likely reason: costs such as rent or salaries have a set size but still rise with prices.
sections.watch_out: The length of the inflation list sets how many years are produced, which may not match the revenue list.

sections.name: calculate_opex_full
sections.title: Totals across all categories
sections.what: Runs each category, stores its results under its name, and adds all categories together for each year.
sections.why: Gives the income statement one total operating expense figure per year.
sections.watch_out: Categories are stored by name, so two categories with the same name overwrite each other.

summary: Works out operating expenses, the costs of running the business apart from goods sold, by category, and adds them into a yearly total.
purpose: Produces the yearly cost of each expense category and the total operating expenses for each year.
why: Operating expenses such as sales, admin, and research costs are a large part of the income statement.
how: 1. For each category, decide whether it is a share of revenue or a fixed amount growing with inflation. 2. Work out that category's yearly values. 3. Store the values under the category name. 4. Add all categories together for each year.
inputs: A revenue list; a list of categories, each with a name, a type (percent_revenue or fixed), and either a percentage or a base amount with inflation rates.
outputs: Yearly values for each category, and the total operating expenses for each year.
risks: Two categories with the same name overwrite each other without a warning. A fixed category shorter than the revenue list is dropped for the missing years without a warning. Fixed base amounts are not divided by a unit divisor, so they must already be in the model's units.
debug: If the total is too low, check for a category missing from the output or two categories sharing a name. If fixed costs look too large or too small, compare their units with revenue.
